Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic HCV (HCV-RNA detectable OR HCV-Ab+ with persistent viremia >6 months) AND no confirmed B-cell NHL diagnosis. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending DAA antiviral therapy (per IND-CHRONIC-HCV-PREVENTION-DAA) as the etiological-cancer-prevention pathway. Evidence for HCV → NHL causation (IARC Group 1): multiple cohort studies show 2-3x increased risk of indolent B-cell NHL in chronic HCV carriers; epidemiology especially robust for MZL subtypes. DAA cure (SVR12) has been associated with reduced NHL incidence in post-treatment cohorts (de-Re et al. and others) and with regression of established HCV-associated indolent NHL (the basis of IND-HCV-MZL-1L-ANTIVIRAL for the treatment persona). This is a STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode exemption (sources cited, draft flag set). Engine consumption is DEFERRED to v0.2 implementation wave — the PreventionPlan code path does not yet exist; this RF lands as schema-valid declarative content awaiting that wave.
Prevention-persona RedFlag combining red: Prevention-persona RedFlag combining red-meat ≥500g/week + processed-meat ≥50g/day thresholds per WCRF/AICR + IARC Monograph 114. Severity:major because processed-meat exposure is Group-1 carcinogen with population-attributable fraction ~13% for CRC (WCRF/AICR). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary substitution + CRC screening per USPSTF. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Coexists with existing RF-LIFESTYLE-PROCESSED-MEAT-PREVENTION — both may fire.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heter: Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heterozygous carriers. Distinction from biallelic A-T phenotype is critical: heterozygotes have cancer predisposition only (no neurologic phenotype). Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance + pancreatic surveillance for FDR-of- PDAC carriers per CAPS consortium 2022; prostate awareness for males. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BAP1 synd: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per la storia della famiglia sindrome BAP1. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BARD1 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BARD1 heterozygous carriers. Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance + ovarian symptom-driven workup. NCCN places BARD1 in moderate-elevated breast tier (annual mammography from age 40; consider MRI). Triple-negative subset signal may justify earlier or MRI-inclusive screening in family- history-stratified cohorts. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BHD/FLCN: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BHD/FLCN confirmed carriers. Multi- organ surveillance: abdominal MRI q2-3y from age 20 for RCC (avoid radiation; many BHD lesions are hybrid oncocytic + slow-growing); chest HRCT baseline + symptom-driven (spontaneous pneumothorax triggers high-resolution imaging); dermatology q1y for skin surveillance. Nephron-sparing surgery (partial nephrectomy) preferred for ≤3cm renal lesions given multifocal/bilateral disease pattern. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BRIP1 het: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per i vettori eterozigoti BRIP1. NCCN approva RRSO alla nascita completa o all'età di 45-50 anni; non è raccomandato uno screening del cancro ovarico della popolazione. Sorveglianza del seno per schemi di popolazione generale a meno che la storia familiare in modo indipendente eleva il rischio. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinens: Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinensis-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. East-Asian endemic belt has 10-50x higher cholangiocarcinoma incidence than non-endemic Western populations. Geographic context: relevant for East-Asian diaspora, immigrants, refugees, adoptees. Companion to RF-OPISTHORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (Mekong-region liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism — identical surveillance protocol).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDH1 / HD: Prevention-persona RedFlag per CDH1 / HDGC confermato vettori per IGCLC 2020 linea guida internazionale. Gastrectomia totale profilattica (PTG) raccomandata età 20-30 (intervallo 18-40 per discussione individualizzata); sorveglianza endoscopica è riconosciuto inferiore a PTG (diffusa-tipo siglet-ring foco cell poco visibile) ma offerto ai vettori PTG-declinarsi. Portatori femminili: BRCA-style seno sorveglianza a partire da 30 anni. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDKN2A-sp: Prevention-persona RedFlag per vettori specifici CDKN2A (RF specifico gene vs il più ampio FAMMM RF). Sorveglianza pancreatica per CAPS Consortium 2018/2020: alternanza EUS + MRI addominale/MRCP ogni 12 mesi dall'età 40 OR 10 anni prima PDAC in famiglia (qualunque precedente). Sorvità melanoma: esame cutaneo annuale a corpo pieno + dermoscopia dall'eta 10-12; mappatura fotografica per molle multiple atipiche. Paziente dovrebbe conoscere la protezione solare aggressiva + coorte specifica CDKNI2A per tutta la vita. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CHEK2 het: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per i vettori eterozigoti CHEK2. Le stime di rischio variano sostanzialmente a seconda delle varianti: trunchi > splice > missenso. Percorsi motori per una sorveglianza mammaria migliorata (mammografia annuale a partire da 40 anni + considerazione di RMN), modestamente stringente screening CRC (colonoscopia a partire dall'età 40 con intervallo q5y per NCCN), e consapevolezza prostata a partire dai 40-45 anni per i maschi con c. 1100delC. STUB in attesa di iscrizione a due Co-Lead per CHARTER § 6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CMMRD con: Prevention-persona RedFlag per CMMRD coorte pediatrica confermata. Sorveglianza per cura per CmmRD (C4CMMRD) consorzio 2014: RMN intero corpo annuale dalla diagnosi; RMC cerebrale q6mo dall'età 2; colonoscopia q6MO dall'eta' 6; endoscopia GI superiore + capsula di piccola bottiglia annua dall' età 8; CBC + elettroforesi proteica sierica + addominale US q6Mo. Test in cascata di fratelli + conferma del supporto parentale MMR. Immunoterapia (anti-PD-1) efficace nei tumori correlati alla CMMRD (Bouffet 2016, serie Larkin/CheckMate). STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for Cronkhite: Prevention-persona RedFlag for Cronkhite-Canada syndrome. risk_category set to chronic_condition (not genetic) because etiology is acquired autoimmune-like + non-Mendelian. Surveillance: colonoscopy q1-2y from diagnosis; upper endoscopy q1-2y; small-bowel capsule q2y; treat active disease with immunosuppression (prednisone taper + azathioprine maintenance) + nutritional support (protein replacement, electrolyte correction). Mortality reduced markedly with immuno- suppression treatment. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DES in-ut: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per la coorte di esposizione inutero DES. La sorveglianza è intensificata rispetto alla popolazione generale (pelvico annuale con attenta ispezione vaginale/cervicale; colposcopia se citologia anormale; mamografia a soglia di età più giovane per NCCN modificatore rischio; considerare la MRI screening aggiunto con doppio rischio). STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DICER1 co: Prevention-persona RedFlag per la coorte confermata di DICER1. Vigilanza pediatrica per Registro PPB internazionale / IDSDB raccomandazioni: - CT toracica q4-6 mo dalla nascita fino ai 3 anni, q6-12 mo fino ai 8 anni, - US abdominale q3-6 mo da nascita a 8 anni. - basale tiroideo US per età 8 + q3-5 y. - US pelvico in portatori femminili da menarche. - base basale di RMI cerebrale + guidata dai sintomi. Chirurgia curativa per PPB tipo I quando rilevata precocemente; PPB avanzato tipo III (componente solido) molto aggressivo. Ooforectomia a rischio-riduttrice non approvata per la prevenzione di Sertoli-Leydig. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-drive: Prevention-persona RedFlag per la prevenzione del cancro guidato da EBV in ospiti immunocompromissi. A differenza dell'HVC/HBV/H. pylori, non esiste un regime anti-EBV curativo; la via di prevenzione è (a) ridurre l'immunosoppressione, ove possibile, (b) rituximab preemptivo in pazienti dopo trapianto con aumento dell'EBV-DNA (per linee guida internazionali di PTLD), (c) monitoraggio periodico dell'ABV-ADN. STUB in attesa di revisione Co-Lead. Il raggio con un contesto di immunocompromesso aggiuntivo è deliberato — la seroprevalenza EBV è >90% negli adulti immunocompetenti a livello globale, quindi un RF attivato su EBW da solo sparerebbe universalmente e non fornirebbe alcun segnale clinico.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for FAMMM / C: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per FAMMM / CDKN2A. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag per la prevenzione del cancro associata al HBV. Incendi su HBsAg+ O rilevabile HB V-DNA in paziente senza HCC. Percorsi motori per PreventionPlan raccomandando la soppressione analogica nucleos(t)ide (per IND-CHRONIC-HBV-PREVENTION-ANTIVIRAL) + AFP+US HCC sorveglianza q6mo per protocollo AASLD. STUB in attesa di revisione Co-Lead. Scopo Cancro: target ancoraggio DIS-HCC. DLBCL/NHL associato al VHB è anche documentato nella letteratura, ma con dati di dimensione dell'effetto più deboli rispetto al collegamento HCV-NHl; coperto attraverso il più ampio proiettile di sorveglianza della prevenzione NHL nella logica dell'indicazione antivirale. Distinto da RF-UNIVERSAL-HBV-REACTIVATION-RISK (esistente) che è il tempo di trattamento RF per la riattivazione del VHBC durante il trattamento anti-CD20 / chemio.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than either mono-infection RF — coinfection carries documented synergistic HCC risk AND DAA-cure-induced HBV reactivation risk that requires combination antiviral. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending concurrent DAA + nucleos(t)ide analog + intensified HCC surveillance (US + AFP q4-6mo, more frequent than the q6mo cadence for either mono-infection). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. NHL prevention (HCV-driven) continues to be a secondary benefit; tracked via prose in the combined-antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HCV-NHL-PREVENTION-OPPORTUNITY and RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence over the two individual RFs (higher priority).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-dri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-driven malignancy prevention. Fires on HHV-8 seropositivity in HIV+, transplant, or other immunocompromised host without confirmed Kaposi sarcoma / MCD / PEL. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending immune restoration (ART for HIV+; transplant-immunosuppression rebalance) + mucocutaneous + oral + GI / lymph-node surveillance. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-KAPOSI. MCD and PEL are HHV-8-driven but not yet authored as distinct Disease entities — covered via the prose surveillance rationale in the indication for now. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (existing) — that is HIV-as-RF; this is HHV-8-positivity-as-RF (the co-factor that turns HIV-related immunocompromise into Kaposi risk specifically).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than mono-infection HBV RF — coinfection carries documented accelerated-fibrosis + elevated HCC risk AND a hard constraint on antiviral selection (tenofovir-based ART mandatory; entecavir monotherapy contraindicated). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending tenofovir-based ART (covers both viruses simultaneously) + AASLD HCC surveillance q6mo. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. HIV-driven AIDS-defining malignancies (Kaposi sarcoma via HHV-8 reactivation, NHL, cervical) are covered separately via RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HHV8-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence (higher priority) and the indication enforces tenofovir-based ART selection.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on positive HIV serology in patient without AIDS-defining or HIV-associated malignancy. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending durable ART suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HIV-PREVENTION-ART) + cancer screening cadence (annual anal cytology in MSM/HIV+; q3-yearly cervical Pap in WLHIV; opportunistic Kaposi/oral hairy leukoplakia visual screening). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the canonical HIV-associated NHL. KS, cervical, anal, Hodgkin, HCC are also HIV-associated; covered via screening recommendations in the ART indication rationale rather than discrete Disease anchors (until DIS-KAPOSI etc. land in v0.2-A authoring backlog).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPRC. STU: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per HPRC. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on persistent high-risk HPV positivity OR incomplete/absent vaccination in age-eligible individual. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending vaccination (Gardasil-9) and/or risk-group-appropriate screening cadence (cervical: USPSTF Pap+HPV co-test q5y ages 30-65; anal: HRA + cytology q1y in MSM/HIV+/post-transplant). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CERVICAL and DIS-ANAL-SCC. Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma and vulvar/vaginal/penile not yet in KB — v0.2-A authoring backlog.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-dr: Prevention-persona RedFlag per la prevenzione ATLL guidata da HTLV-1. A differenza dell'HCV/HBV/h. pylori, non esiste un regime curativo — l'intervento è la sorveglianza + prevenzione della trasmissione, non la cura. STUB in attesa di revisione Co-Lead. Contesto geografico: le regioni endemiche HTV-1 includono il Giappone (sud-ovest), bacino dei Caraibi, parti dell'Africa sub-sahariana, parti del Sud America, Medio Oriente. L'Ucraina è bassa prevalenza; questa RF è più rilevante per i pazienti con diaspora o quelli con viaggi / origine da regioni endemiche.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 the: Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 therapeutic-dose lifetime cumulative exposure. Surveillance: CBC q12mo for leukemia signal (sensitivity modest); breast surveillance per general-population USPSTF unless additional risk factors; oral + salivary symptom awareness. Highest-impact preventive intervention is hydration + lemon-juice sialagogue during I-131 administration (reduces salivary gland uptake) — retrospectively non-actionable for prior exposure. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAF: Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAFLD HCC risk. Cirrhotic MASLD meets AASLD HCC-surveillance threshold (US ± AFP q6mo). Non-cirrhotic advanced fibrosis is a gray zone — closer hepatology follow-up but not yet routine surveillance. Major actionable lever: weight loss + cardiometabolic management. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confi: Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confirmed-carrier / clinical- diagnostic-criteria-met cohort. Multi-organ surveillance: pediatric ophthalmology q6-12mo to age 8 (optic glioma); whole-body MRI for MPNST surveillance + symptom-driven biopsy of growing/painful/ neurologically-symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas; women: annual mammography from age 30, MRI from age 30-50. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverrini-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. Northeast Thailand has the world's highest cholangiocarcinoma incidence (up to 90 per 100K) — attributable fraction in endemic regions exceeds 50%. Geographic context: relevant for Mekong-region diaspora, refugees, travelers, and adoptees. Companion to RF-CLONORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (East Asian liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 het: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per PALB2 eterozigoti vettori. PALb2 approccia BRCA2 penetranza tumorale al seno e giustifica la sorveglianza in stile BRCA con RMI mammaria annuale + mammografia a partire da 30 anni, più sorveglianza pancreatica (EUS o RMI alternando annualmente a partire dall'età 50, o 10 anni prima PDAC in famiglia) per FDR-of-PDAC vettori per consorzio CAPS 2022. Discussione RRSO rinviato a soglia in stile BRCA dato la penetranza ovarica inferiore. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anov: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per PCOS-anovulation rischio endometriale. Separato dalla RF riproduttiva ampia per un incamminamento più chiaro — consulenza specifica per PCO (ripristino della progestina, metformina, perdita di peso) è distinta da consulente generico riproduzione-historia. Biopsia endometriale azionata da simptomi in qualsiasi sanguinamento anormale ≥6 mesi di amenorrea pre-menopausale O qualsiasi sanguinamento post-menopatopausa. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RA: Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RAD51D heterozygous carriers. Approaches BRCA-level ovarian penetrance — NCCN endorses RRSO at completed childbearing or age 45-50. Breast surveillance: individualised by family history; consider annual MRI in additional- risk subset. Olaparib PARP inhibitor active in RAD51C/D-mutant established ovarian cancer (PROfound + GEN-ALL trials). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haemat: Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haematobium-driven bladder SCC prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifetime urinary surveillance (urinalysis q6-12mo, cytology + cystoscopy for any new hematuria). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL. S. haematobium-driven bladder cancers are predominantly SCC histology (distinct from urothelial / transitional cell carcinoma that dominates Western cohorts) — engine surfaces this distinction in the prevention rationale prose. Geographic context: Ukraine is non-endemic; this RF is relevant for patients with diaspora / refugee / travel / origin history from sub-Saharan Africa, Egypt, Sudan, Yemen, parts of South America.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for SDH-defic: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per la sindrome da deficit SDH. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for active to: Prevention-persona RedFlag per l'uso attivo del tabacco. Intervento modificabile del cancro-rischio-fattore di massimo impatto. Percorsi motori a PreventionPlan raccomandando consulenza strutturata di cessazione + farmacoterapia + screening polmonare LDCT se ammissibile USPSTF. STUB in attesa di due-clinica-Co-Lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracyc: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per antraciclina dose cumulativa ≥250 mg/m2. Focus di sorveglianza cardio-cardiologica (HF / cardiomiopatia); sovrapposizione di sorveglianza t-AML coperta da RF-IATROGENIC-TOPO2-TAML-PREVENTION separata. Echo q1-5y a seconda del profilo di rischio (Cadenza ASCO/COG-LTFU). Percorsi motori verso PreventionPlan raccomandando basale + eco seriale + BNP. STUB in attesa di iscrizione a due clinici-Co-Lead per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per aromatici-ammine → prevenzione del cancro alla vescica uroteliale. Incendio su esposizione professionale documentata. ancoraggio DIS-UROTHELIAL preferito ma utilizzando DIS-HCC come ritocco se non in KB su questo ramo. STUB in attesa di due-clinica-Co-Lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic E: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ETS exposure (household / workplace ≥10y). IARC Group 1 + US Surgeon General-confirmed cause of lung cancer in non-smokers. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum. Distinct from active-smoking RF. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure elimination (cohabitant smoking cessation / workplace smoke-free policy enforcement / personal mitigation) + USPSTF screening eligibility check + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic P: Prevention-persona RedFlag per l'esposizione cronica PPI ≥10y. Percorsi motori a PreventionPlan raccomanda (1) indicazione-revisione + disprescription dove il PPI non è più necessario (scenario più comune), (2) gastrine a digiuno + cromogranina A in coorte con indicazione persistente di antiacido, (3) EGD con biopsie corpo/fondo in quelli con gastrin o sintomi elevati; sorveglianza EGd q3-5y se gastrite atrofica o iperplasia ECL documentata. Assegnato a DIS-GASTRIC (neto gastrico e adenocarcinoma derivato da atrofiti-gastrite sia malattie gastrica-corpali); esito specifico di NE portato in prosa indicativa. STUB in attesa di due-clinico-co-lead firma per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic a: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic anti-TNF biologic exposure ≥3y in pediatric / adolescent / young-adult IBD cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) EBV serology baseline in young adults, (2) B-symptom + lymphadenopathy awareness, (3) annual skin examination (synergistic with concomitant thiopurine + UV), (4) periodic shared-decision discussion of combination- therapy step-down where IBD activity allows (anti-TNF monotherapy has favourable cancer signal vs combination with thiopurine), (5) vaccination catch-up (HPV, HBV, influenza, pneumococcal). Severity = minor — absolute attributable risk in anti-TNF monotherapy is small; the meaningful signal is the combination- with-thiopurine HSTCL warning specifically in pediatric / young- adult cohort, addressed via combination-step-down counseling. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS + DIS-HSTCL. STUB pending two-Clinical- Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic i: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic inorganic arsenic exposure via drinking water >10 µg/L (WHO + US EPA MCL). IARC Group 1 carcinogen with established urothelial, lung, and non-melanoma skin cancer etiology. Anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL per task brief; lung + skin surfaced via relevant_diseases. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending water source change / filtration + intensified screening for affected organs. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic o: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic occupational outdoor UV exposure ≥10y in high-UV-index latitudes. IARC Group 1 solar UV. Distinct from broader RF-LIFESTYLE-UV-EXPOSURE-PREVENTION (which covers tanning beds + sunburn history + recreational UV). Anchored to DIS-BCC per task brief (closest skin DIS to UV-NMSC). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending photoprotection counseling + clinical skin exam cadence + patient skin self-exam education + Vitamin D balance. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic p: Prevenzione-persona RedFlag per la pancreatite cronica → PDAC. Pancreatiti ereditaria porta il rischio più alto (~40-50% vita). STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic r: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic residential PM2.5 >35 µg/m³ annual average (WHO 2021 IT-1). IARC Group 1 outdoor air pollution + PM. Population-attributable fraction modest individually but large absolute burden in high-exposure regions including industrial Ukraine + during war-related fire / debris events. risk_category=occupational is the closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum (§20 ratification pending). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure reduction + USPSTF lung-cancer screening eligibility + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥3y post-transplant immunosuppression cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan with long-cycle surveillance cadence appropriate to the chronic cohort (vs the acute-window EBV-DNA cadence in the new-transplant RF). Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TRANSPLANT-IMMUNOSUPPRESSION- PREVENTION (which covers acute / new-transplant window). Both RFs may fire simultaneously in the early-chronic window (1-3y post-transplant) — engine routes to both surveillance tracks, render layer deduplicates overlapping recommendations. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the primary lymphoma anchor (late- onset PTLD histology more DLBCL-like; DIS-PTLD as the canonical early-onset EBV-driven entity). Multiple cancer types listed in relevant_diseases reflect the broad cumulative-risk profile of the chronic cohort. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined: Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined HRT exposure ≥5y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) shared-decision discussion of risk-benefit (vasomotor symptoms, bone-density preservation vs breast / VTE / cardiovascular risks), (2) lowest-effective-dose + shortest-duration principle per NAMS / ACOG, (3) breast surveillance per USPSTF cadence — supplemental imaging not recommended on HRT alone (density-related supplemental imaging is a separate axis), (4) symptom-prompted endometrial workup (any abnormal bleeding → TVUS + biopsy) for women on sequential/cyclic combined or with intact uterus on any HRT, (5) annual GYN exam. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TAMOXIFEN-ENDOMETRIAL-PREVENTION (different mechanism: SERM with partial endometrial agonism). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Primary IO resistance is operationally d: Primary IO resistance is operationally distinct from acquired resistance (PD after initial response >6 months). SITC consensus (Kluger 2020) defines primary resistance as PD within 6 months of IO start. Subsequent options vary by tumor: melanoma — BRAF/MEKi if V600E, T-VEC, TIL therapy at trial centers, IL-2; NSCLC — docetaxel ± ramucirumab, ADC if HER2/TROP2; urothelial — enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab combination remains active even after IO-mono PD per EV-302; RCC — cabozantinib monotherapy or lenvatinib + everolimus. IO-rechallenge is generally not standard but may be considered after >6 months treatment-free + non-PD discontinuation reason.

Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) — confirmed by characteristic cholangiographic findings on MRCP or ERCP (multifocal intra-/extra- hepatic biliary strictures with intervening dilatation, beaded appearance) and/or liver biopsy (concentric periductal fibrosis, onion-skin pattern). Includes PSC-IBD subgroup (very high risk for both CRC and cholangiocarcinoma) and PSC with dominant biliary stricture (additional cholangiocarcinoma risk requiring focused diagnostic workup). No current cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, or HCC diagnosis. PSC is the strongest known risk factor for cholangiocarcinoma — lifetime risk ~10-15% (vs ~0.01% in general population); annual incidence ~0.5-1.5% per year. Prodrug activated by hepatic CYP2B6/CYP3: Profarmaceutica attivata dal CYP2B6/CYP3A4 epatico alla senape fosforamide, che collega i fili del DNA e induce l'apoptosi. Attiva sia nelle cellule proliferanti che in riposo; ampiamente usata nelle neoplasmie linfoide.
Prodrug hydrolyzed by carboxylesterases: Prodrug idrolizzati dalle carboxilesterasi al metabolita attivo SN-38 (~100-1000× più potente del genitore). SN‐38 stabilizza il complesso di topoisomerasi-I/DNA scioglievole, producendo rotture di DNA a singolo filamento che diventano rotture letali a doppio filamento durante la replicazione in fase S. SN-38 è glucuronidato da UGT1A1 a SN -38G inattivo; i pazienti omozigoti per UGt1A 1*28 (variante Gilbert-sindrome) o *6 hanno una clearance ridotta e una neutropenia severa + rischio di diarrea - l'etichetta CPIC e FDA raccomandano entrambi i test prima dell'uso di dosi elevate.
Prodrug requiring hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B: Prodrug requiring hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B6 activation to 4-hydroxy- ifosfamide, which decomposes to ifosforamide mustard — the active DNA- alkylating species producing N7-guanine inter-strand crosslinks and apoptosis in proliferating cells. Side-chain oxidation also generates acrolein (urotoxic — drives hemorrhagic cystitis, neutralized by mesna) and chloroacetaldehyde (the principal neurotoxic metabolite responsible for ifosfamide-induced encephalopathy).
Prodrug that is acid-activated in the pa: Prodrug that is acid-activated in the parietal cell secretory canaliculus to a sulfenamide cation, which forms a covalent disulfide bond with cysteine residues of the H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump) and irreversibly inhibits gastric acid secretion. New pump synthesis is required for recovery (≥24 h half-life of effect despite ~1 h plasma half-life). Cancer-prevention relevance: profound gastric acid suppression is required for H. pylori antimicrobial efficacy (clarithromycin and amoxicillin both require near-neutral gastric pH for stability and bactericidal activity) — PPI is the linchpin of triple / quadruple H. pylori eradication regimens.

Provides supplemental elemental calcium: Provides supplemental elemental calcium (~40% by mass of calcium carbonate). Absorbed in proximal small bowel via active vitamin-D- dependent transcellular transport (saturable at low calcium intake) and passive paracellular diffusion (linear with concentration). Cancer-prevention rationale: intraluminal calcium binds free bile acids and free fatty acids in the colon, reducing their proliferative and pro-inflammatory effect on colonic mucosa; additionally calcium modulates epithelial cell proliferation/differentiation via the calcium-sensing receptor. Calcium Polyp Prevention Study (Baron NEJM 1999) and follow-on trials: 1200 mg/day elemental calcium reduced metachronous adenoma recurrence by ~15-20%.

Pyrexia (especially dabrafenib + trameti: Pyrexia (especially dabrafenib + trametinib) is the dominant BRAF+MEK toxicity — patient education + dose-hold algorithm essential. Encorafenib + binimetinib has lower pyrexia but higher CK elevation. Adjuvant dabrafenib + trametinib (COMBI-AD) for stage III BRAF-mut resected melanoma. Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly conve: Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly converted to FdUMP, FdUTP, and FUTP. FdUMP forms a stable ternary complex with thymidylate synthase (TS) + reduced folate (leucovorin), depleting dTMP and blocking DNA synthesis. FUTP misincorporation into RNA disrupts pre-mRNA processing; FdUTP misincorporation into DNA produces strand breaks. Backbone of FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, FOLFIRINOX, FLOT, and capecitabine-bridged regimens. Bolus and continuous-infusion (CIV) schedules differ in toxicity profile (more myelosuppression with bolus, more mucositis/HFS with CIV).
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporate: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporated into DNA and RNA, inhibits DNA methyltransferases → re-expression of silenced tumor-suppressor genes + cytotoxicity at higher doses. Backbone of MDS-HR, AML-unfit (with venetoclax), and CMML 1L therapy.
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycyt: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycytidine. Phosphorylated by deoxycytidine kinase (rate-limiting) to active metabolites gemcitabine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and triphosphate (dFdCTP). dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, depleting deoxynucleotide pools required for DNA synthesis (self-potentiation effect — increases cellular dFdCTP). dFdCTP is incorporated into DNA, after which one additional natural nucleotide is added before DNA polymerase stalls — "masked chain termination" — making the lesion resistant to exonucleolytic repair. Cell cycle phase-specific (S phase) with G1/S blockade. PDAC backbone (gem-nab-pac MPACT, gem mono in frail), biliary tract cancers, NSCLC, bladder, NK/T-nasal lymphoma (SMILE), Hodgkin / DLBCL salvage (GDP).
Pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that, after: Antifolato di pirrolopirimidina che, dopo poliglutamazione intracellulare da folilpoliglutamato sintetasi, inibisce contemporaneamente i più enzimi dipendenti dal folato critici per la timidina e la biosintesi della purina: timidilato sintetosi (TS — bersaglio primario), diidrofolato reductasi (DHFR) e glicinamide ribonucleotide formiltransferasi (GARFT). L'inibizione combinata interrompe sia la sintesi del timidinato che della purine de-novo, sospendendo la produzione di DNA/RNA e producendo citotossicità specifica in fase S. L'attività è limitata all'istologia: altamente attiva in NSCLC non squamoso e mesotelioma pleurico maligno (MPM); minima a nessuna attività in NCSLC squamatoso a causa di una maggiore espressione basale di TS in istologia squamosa. L'aggiunta obbligatoria di acido folico (vitamina B9) e vitamina B12 riduce la tossicità ematologica e mucosa di ~50% senza compromettere l'efficacia (Niyikiza 2002, Vogelzang EMPHACIS).

Quantitative HBV DNA tracks response during nucleos(t)ide-analogue (NA) therapy with entecavir (ETV) or tenofovir alafenamide/disoproxil (TAF/TDF). Effective suppression (HBV DNA <2,000 IU/mL, ideally undetectable) is the primary virologic response endpoint per AASLD HBV 2024 and EASL HBV 2025. Sustained suppression reduces HCC incidence by ~50-70% in CHB cirrhotics (REVEAL-HBV cohort; Wong 2013 meta-analysis). Primary non-response or viral breakthrough (≥1-log rise on therapy) prompts adherence review, resistance testing, and regimen change (rare with ETV/TAF/TDF — high genetic barrier). ESCAT IIIA — biomarker directs antiviral continuation/switch decisions and is the primary HCC-prevention lever in chronic HBV.
Quantitative HBV DNA used to TRACK viral: Quantitative HBV DNA used to TRACK viral suppression over time during chronic-HBV antiviral therapy (entecavir or tenofovir TDF/TAF — first- line nucleos(t)ide analogues per AASLD 2024 / EASL 2025). Distinct from BIO-HBV-STATUS (serology-based screening / treatment-decision gate). Two clinical contexts: (1) Treatment monitoring in HBeAg+/HBeAg− chronic HBV: baseline HBV DNA + ALT + HBeAg + HBsAg → start NA → recheck q3 months for first year, then q6 months. Goal: HBV DNA undetectable on treatment; ALT normalization; HBeAg seroconversion (HBeAg+ patients) or HBsAg loss (functional cure — rare on NA monotherapy, ~1% per year). Virologic breakthrough (≥1-log rise from nadir) prompts adherence review then switch (entecavir → tenofovir if NA-naïve resistance). (2) Prophylaxis monitoring during B-cell-depleting therapy (rituximab, obinutuzumab) or anti-CD38 (daratumumab, isatuximab) in HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients: entecavir prophylaxis baseline → HBV DNA q3 months during chemotherapy and for 12+ months post-treatment; any detectable HBV DNA = reactivation, hepatology consult. R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AM: R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AML (~70-80% of IDH2-mut AML; ~6-8% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved Aug 2017 for R/R-AML-IDH2 monotherapy (phase 1/2: ORR 38%, CR 19%). 1L combination with azacitidine in unfit patients (AG221-AML-005: ORR 71%). Differentiation syndrome (~14%) — same monitoring + dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib. Hyperbilirubinemia (~80% any grade; UGT1A1 inhibition — usually asymptomatic, no dose adjustment unless symptomatic). IDHENTIFY R/R AML phase-3 did not show OS benefit vs conventional care over all comers but enriched in IDH2-mut who had not received prior HMA. Combination with venetoclax + azacitidine under study. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML: R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML (~20-30% of IDH2-mut AML; ~2-3% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved across both R140 and R172 variants. Some series (Stein et al., Blood 2017) suggest R172K carries lower CR rate than R140Q on enasidenib mono, but still substantial activity. Differentiation syndrome (~14%) and hyperbilirubinemia same as R140Q. Glioma IDH2 R172K is a separate clinical entity (vorasidenib INDIGO trial) — this biomarker is AML-scoped; glioma IDH2 captured under BIO-IDH-MUTATION composite. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R175H is the most common TP53 missense h: R175H is the most common TP53 missense hotspot across all human cancers (~5-7% of TP53-mutant tumors per IARC TP53 Database). Structural class mutant — the R175 substitution to histidine disrupts the DNA-binding domain fold (zinc-coordination region). Beyond loss-of-function (LoF), R175H is a canonical example of mutant-p53 GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (GOF): the mutant protein acquires pro-oncogenic activities (chemoresistance via NF-kB, increased migration/invasion, metabolic reprogramming, chronic inflammation). Clinical implication: R175H+ tumors generally have worse chemo response than TP53-WT or even other TP53-mut tumors. In AML: TP53-mut (any) including R175H → very poor outcomes with intensive chemo, route to alloSCT or venetoclax-azacitidine + clinical trials. In MM: routes to quadruplet per high-risk cytogenetics composite. Emerging GOF-targeting strategies (eprenetapopt/APR-246, arsenic trioxide for structural mutants) are largely investigational; R175H specifically among the reactivatable structural mutants.
R248 is one of the six most-mutated codo: R248 is one of the six most-mutated codons in TP53 (along with R175, G245, R249, R273, R282). DNA-contact class: R248 sits in the L3 loop and makes direct base-specific contact with the DNA minor groove. Substitution to glutamine (R248Q) abolishes sequence-specific DNA binding while preserving overall fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H). R248Q has well-documented gain-of-function (GOF) activities in mouse models — accelerates tumorigenesis and metastasis beyond simple p53-null. Clinical implications mirror other TP53 hotspots: in AML/MDS routes away from intensive chemo toward venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT; in CLL/MCL/MM contraindicates chemoimmuno or routes to high-risk-cytogenetics regimens. Distinction from R248W (different substitution, also a hotspot) — R248Q tends to retain partial folding while R248W more disruptive; both are pathogenic.
R273 is among the top three most-mutated: R273 is among the top three most-mutated TP53 codons (with R175 and R248). DNA-contact class: R273 directly contacts the DNA major groove via its guanidinium side chain. R→H substitution preserves the thermal stability of the protein fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H) but eliminates specific DNA binding. R273H is one of the best-characterized GOF p53 mutants — promotes chemoresistance via NF-κB activation, drives invasion/metastasis through CXCR4 and RhoA pathways, reprograms metabolism (mevalonate pathway upregulation). Clinical implications mirror the TP53-mutant class: AML/MDS — venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; CLL/MCL — contraindicates chemoimmuno; MM — high-risk cytogenetics composite routes to quadruplet. Notably, R273H tumors are particularly resistant to platinum chemotherapy across solid-tumor types per multiple correlative analyses — relevant for ovarian, lung, esophageal cancer treatment selection.
R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codo: R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codon, often grouped with R248 and R273 as the canonical hotspot ring. Hybrid structural/contact mutant: R282 stabilizes the L1/S3 loop region adjacent to the DNA-binding surface, and R→W partially destabilizes the fold while altering contact geometry. Functional studies show R282W retains partial transactivation activity on a subset of canonical p53 targets (CDKN1A/p21, BBC3/PUMA at reduced levels) — termed "partial LoF" — while still gaining oncogenic activities. Clinically R282W behaves similarly to other hotspots: in AML/MDS poor chemo response → routes to venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; in CLL/MCL/MM high-risk regimen routing. Distinction from full LoF mutants (truncating, splice-site) may matter for emerging mutant-p53 reactivator drugs (eprenetapopt) where residual fold is required — R282W generally considered reactivatable in early-phase trials.

RADIANT-3 (Yao NEJM 2011): everolimus 10: RADIANT-3 (Yao NEJM 2011): everolimus 10 mg/day vs placebo in progressive well-differentiated pNET (n=410). mPFS 11.0 vs 4.6 mo (HR 0.35, p<0.001). No significant OS benefit demonstrated (confounded by >70% crossover post- progression). SSA prior / concurrent use allowed. Stomatitis prophylaxis (dexamethasone mouthwash, SWISH trial) reduces G2+ stomatitis dramatically. Sunitinib 37.5 mg/day is the alternative (Raymond NEJM 2011 — similar mPFS 11.4 vs 5.5 mo, HR 0.42); no head-to-head comparison; choice based on comorbidities (cardiac/renal → prefer everolimus; diabetes/steroids → consider sunitinib). STUB pending §6.1 signoff.
RAI-refractory PTC TKI therapy is multi-: La terapia con PTC TKI refrattaria RAI è pluriennale (mediana PFS 18 mo su lenvatinib SELECT; >25 mo su selpercatinib LIBRETTO) — l'esposizione cronica aumenta il rischio di riattivazione del VHB. RB1 alterations (deletion, mutation) occur in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and are enriched in the basal/squamous-differentiated molecular subtype (~50%). RB1 loss is associated with resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (which require pRb to exert G1 arrest). In urothelial cancer, CDK4/6 inhibitors are investigational (no approved indication); however, RB1 status is being evaluated as a predictive biomarker for CDK4/6 inhibitor non-response in HR+ cancers where bladder patients are enrolled in basket trials. Therapeutic implications in bladder cancer: (1) RB1 loss may associate with sensitivity to immunotherapy (higher genomic instability) — inconsistent evidence; (2) Basal/squamous subtype (often RB1-low) responds better to neoadjuvant chemotherapy than luminal subtypes; (3) No approved targeted therapy exploits RB1 deficiency in bladder cancer as of 2026. ESCAT IIIB: RB1 is a prognostic and potential therapeutic vulnerability marker in urothelial cancer; no approved targeted agent.

RB1 biallelic loss, together with TP53 loss, is the molecular hallmark of SCLC (~95% of cases have both). RB1 loss is not used to select therapy in SCLC (all SCLC patients receive the same backbone: EP/EC ± atezolizumab/durvalumab); rather, it is a diagnostic characteristic and potential therapeutic vulnerability. RB1 loss renders cells dependent on alternative cell cycle regulators (CDK4/6-independent E2F activation) — this is why CDK4/6 inhibitors have no activity in SCLC (pRb loss negates CDK4/6 inhibition). Investigational targeting of RB1-deficient SCLC: aurora kinase A inhibitors (alisertib — phase II, limited activity); EZH2 inhibitors (tazemetostat — RB1-null tumors may have heightened EZH2 dependence); LSD1 inhibitors; ATR/CHK1 inhibitors (replication stress in RB1-null context). ESCAT IIIB: RB1 loss is diagnostically informative and a conceptual therapeutic target, but no FDA-approved targeted therapy exploiting RB1 deficiency as of 2026.
RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (: RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (pRb), the master G1/S checkpoint regulator. pRb normally sequesters E2F transcription factors to prevent S-phase entry; loss of pRb → uncontrolled cell cycle progression. Clinical contexts: (1) Hereditary retinoblastoma: germline RB1 mutation → bilateral/multifocal retinoblastoma in childhood; lifetime elevated risk of osteosarcoma, SCLC, melanoma. (2) SCLC: biallelic RB1 loss + TP53 mutation defines the SCLC molecular signature (~95% of SCLC). pRb loss by IHC is used in pathologic diagnosis. No targeted therapy for RB1 deficiency per se; SCLC treatment is chemotherapy (EP/EC) ± atezolizumab. (3) Urothelial carcinoma: RB1 alterations in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer; associated with basal/squamous subtype; not currently targeted. (4) Breast cancer: RB1 mutations occur in ~10% of TNBC; RB1 loss predicts resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib) — pRb is the substrate for CDK4/6 that drives cell cycle entry; without pRb, CDK4/6 inhibition is ineffective. I vettori affrontano a vita ~50% rischio di tumori primari secondari (osteosarcoma, sarcoma di tessuto molle, melanoma, polmone, vescica); rischio cumulativo marcatamente elevato dopo la radioterapia a fascio esterno (EBRT) — i protocolli moderni evitano EBRT per attenuare. Protocollo di sorveglianza confermato (per COG / Children's Oncology Group + International Retinoblastoma Consorzio): oftalmologia pediatrica con UCE (esame sotto anestesia) a partire dal periodo neonato — ogni 2-4 settimane fino all'età 1, poi progressivo allungamento mensile → q3mo → q6mo fino all 'età 7, annuale fino all`adolescenza. Test in cascata a tutti i parenti di primo grado obbligatori. Monitoraggio di lunga vita del cancro secondario: esame cutaneo annuale, attenzione al dolore osseo (osteosarcoma nell'adolescenza/giovane adulti), evitazione di irradiazioni ionizzanti diagnostiche inutili. ESCAT IIA.

Radiotherapy contraindicated or declined for early-stage NLPBL (nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma, WHO 5th ed). Major clinical scenarios: (1) Young patient with breast or thyroid field overlap — cumulative RT dose risk of secondary malignancy and cardiac toxicity unacceptable; (2) Prior RT to the involved or adjacent region — reirradiation risks exceed benefit; (3) Patient refuses RT after informed discussion. In all scenarios rituximab monotherapy (4–8 × R weekly) achieves ~94% ORR with ≥70% CR in early-stage NLPBL (Advani 2014, IELSG-37 data) and is the accepted standard alternative. RT remains the default for eligible patients where field is safe and patient consents (stage IA-IIA, ≤2 cm).

Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose d: Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone until progression) was the MAIA control arm (Facon NEJM 2019, PMID 30926586) and represents the standard-access first-line regimen for transplant-ineligible NDMM. MAIA control arm outcomes: ORR 75.8%, PFS HR (D-Rd vs Rd) 0.56 (95% CI 0.43–0.73), 30-month PFS ~53.3% for D-Rd vs ~37.8% for Rd. Rd continuous showed superiority over MPT and melphalan-prednisone in the FIRST trial (Benboubker NEJM 2014, PMID 25184863): PFS 26 months vs 21.9 months for MPT. Dose of dexamethasone: low-dose (40 mg weekly = "Ld schedule") is preferred over high-dose (480 mg/cycle); ECOG E4A03 showed equivalent efficacy and better tolerability with low-dose dex in NDMM (Rajkumar LANCET ONCOL 2010). Recombinant non-infectious nine-valent H: Recombinant non-infectious nine-valent HPV vaccine. L1 VLPs are immunogenic but contain no viral DNA — cannot cause HPV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer neutralizing IgG that prevents incident infection by the covered HPV types. Cancer-prevention pathway: prevents persistent infection with the HPV types responsible for ~90% of cervical cancers, ~90% of anal cancers, ~70% of vaginal/vulvar cancers, ~60% of penile cancers, and a growing fraction of oropharyngeal cancers.

Co-occurring resistance markers include AR-V7 splice variant, AR LBD point mutations (L702H, T878A, F877L), and lineage plasticity (neuroendocrine transformation). Priority 76 chosen to fall just below RF-PROSTATE-AR-V7-ARSI-RESISTANCE (75) — both are informational and complementary; AR-V7 evidence (PROPHECY) prospectively validated, AR-amp evidence largely retrospective ctDNA cohorts. KB scope choice: ships as biomarker + RF (informational) only — no new IND, no algorithm step. Tx-modifying signal deferred to a future taxane-mCRPC IND chunk that branches on AR-amp / AR-V7 / LBD-mutation status.

Consumo regolare di maté (Ilex paraguariensis infusione) preparato e bevuto a temperature molto alte (≥65°C / ≥149°F) - caratteristico della tradizionale preparazione di gurda e bombarda nel Sud America (Argentina, Brasile, Paraguay, Uruguay, Cile meridionale) e comunità di diaspora. IARC Monograph 116 (2016) classificato come gruppo 2A (probabilmente cancerogeno) il consumo di bevande molto calde a partire da 65°C — evidenza limitata nell'uomo (associazione coerente con carcinoma squamoso esofageo nelle cohorte di bevute, tè caldo e caffè caldo, con confondenza residua da co-esposizione tabacco/alcol non completamente esclusa), evidenze sufficienti negli animali sperimentali (lesione termica → infiammazione cronica → carcinogenesi di campo nei modelli esofagici di roditori). Importante: a temperature <60°C non si osserva alcuna associazione; il maté per se (l'erba / i suoi fitochimici) NON è classificato come cancerogeno...
Regular consumption of very hot beverage: Regular consumption of very hot beverages (≥65°C / 149°F) per IARC Monograph 116 (2016) — applies primarily to teas (especially traditional preparation styles in regions of Iran, Turkey, China, parts of South America with maté), but also coffee/water consumed at scalding temperatures. IARC Group 2A (probably carcinogenic) classification — associated with esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma (ESCC), particularly in regions with high background ESCC incidence. Mechanism: thermal injury to esophageal epithelium → chronic inflammation → field carcinogenesis. Note: at typical Western coffee/tea temperatures (<60°C), no association observed; coffee + tea per se are not carcinogenic. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g: Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g/day per WCRF/IARC threshold. IARC Monograph 114 (2015) classified processed meat as Group 1 carcinogen for colorectal cancer (sufficient evidence). Each 50 g/day of processed meat increases CRC risk by ~18% (meta-analyzed RR ~1.18; WCRF/AICR convincing-evidence rating). Processed meat = sausages, ham, bacon, salami, cured/smoked/salted/preserved meat. Red meat (Group 2A per IARC, probable carcinogen) is a separate but overlapping concern — threshold ≥500 g/week for red meat. Mechanisms: N-nitroso compounds, heterocyclic amines, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, heme iron. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Relapsed/refractory DLBCL with confirmed CD20 expression on malignant B-cells, post ≥2 prior systemic therapies including one anti-CD20 antibody-containing regimen (R-CHOP), CAR-T-ineligible or post-CAR-T failure — candidate for epcoritamab (CD20xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager; subcutaneous step-up administration). Pivotal data EPCORE NHL-1 phase 1/2 (Thieblemont 2023 J Clin Oncol): ORR 63%, CR 39%, mPFS 4.4 mo, mDOR 12 mo in 3L+ R/R DLBCL. Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T for non-eligible / bridging / post-failure setting. Distinct from glofitamab (different schedule: fixed 12 cycles vs continuous; IV vs SC). CD20-loss escape post-prior-anti-CD20 is a documented mechanism — re-biopsy advisable for late-relapse cohorts.

Relapsed/refractory DLBCL with confirmed CD20 expression on malignant B-cells, post ≥2 prior systemic therapies including one anti-CD20 antibody-containing regimen (R-CHOP), CAR-T-ineligible or post-CAR-T failure — candidate for glofitamab (CD20xCD3 2:1 bispecific T-cell engager; intravenous; fixed 12-cycle duration). Pivotal data NP30179 phase 1/2 (Dickinson 2022 NEJM): ORR 52%, CR 39%, mPFS 4.9 mo, mDOR 18.4 mo in 3L+ R/R DLBCL after fixed treatment course. Differentiator vs epcoritamab: fixed-duration (12 cycles ≈ 8.3 mo) vs continuous; IV vs SC; obinutuzumab pre-treatment 7 days before C1D1 reduces CRS. Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T. Often considered after epcoritamab failure in BiTE-sequencing strategies, though direct comparative data are lacking.

Reproductive history combining late first full-term pregnancy (age ≥30) OR nulliparity, AND short cumulative lifetime breastfeeding duration (<6 months total). Both factors independently confer modest increases in hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer risk (RR ~1.2-1.4 each) per Collaborative Group on Hormonal Factors in Breast Cancer + WCRF/AICR. Breastfeeding is protective in dose- dependent fashion (~4% breast cancer risk reduction per 12 months of cumulative breastfeeding). Mechanism: cumulative ovulatory cycles + unopposed estrogen exposure + delayed terminal differentiation of breast ductal epithelium. Effect cumulative with other reproductive factors (early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, HRT). Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 reproductive pilot).

Reversible non-steroidal inhibitor of cy: Reversible non-steroidal inhibitor of cytochrome P450 aromatase (CYP19A1), reducing peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogens (estradiol, estrone). In postmenopausal women aromatase activity in adipose, breast, and other peripheral tissue is the dominant estrogen source — anastrozole 1 mg/day suppresses circulating estradiol by ~80-95%. Cancer-prevention rationale: estrogen exposure is the dominant driver of HR-positive breast carcinogenesis, and near-complete suppression of postmenopausal estrogen production reduces incidence of ER-positive breast cancer (and DCIS). IBIS-II RCT (Cuzick Lancet 2014, 12-year follow-up Lancet 2020): in 3,864 postmenopausal high-risk women, anastrozole 1 mg/day for 5 years reduced breast-cancer incidence by ~49% vs. placebo (HR 0.51) with durable benefit out to 12 years.

Also part of the IMspire150 triplet (atezolizumab + cobimetinib + vemurafenib) for previously untreated BRAF V600 advanced melanoma, where the addition of atezolizumab modestly extended PFS. Revumenib (SNDX-5613), an oral menin inhibitor, is FDA-approved (Nov 2024) for relapsed/refractory KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemia (AML and ALL). AUGMENT-101 (Issa et al. NEJM 2023; Erba et al. ASH 2023 update): KMT2A-rearranged R/R AML/ALL — ORR 23% (CR + CRh + CRi), complete remission with full recovery 18%; mOS 8.0 mo. FDA accelerated approval based on remission rate as surrogate endpoint. KMT2A rearrangement is present in ~10% of adult AML (more common in secondary/therapy-related AML and infant leukemia). Menin is an essential co-factor of KMT2A-fusion oncoproteins — revumenib disrupts menin-MLL interaction, restoring differentiation block. Combination strategies under evaluation: revumenib + venetoclax + azacitidine (phase II ongoing). ELN 2022 risk: KMT2A-rearranged AML classified as intermediate risk (specific partner-dependent — MLLT3 intermediate; others may be adverse).

Revumenib (menin inhibitor) FDA-approved (Nov 2024) for relapsed/refractory KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemia including B-ALL. AUGMENT-101 combined KMT2A-rearranged cohort (AML + ALL): ORR 23%, CR/CRh 18%. KMT2A rearrangement defines a high-risk B-ALL subset: in infants KMT2A-AFF1 is present in ~80% of infant B-ALL (EFS <30% with standard chemotherapy); in adults KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL is adverse-risk (NCCN/ELN). Revumenib represents a first targeted option for this historically chemotherapy-refractory population. Blinatumomab (CD19 BiTE, FDA-approved for R/R B-ALL) and inotuzumab ozogamicin are also active in KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL regardless of KMT2A status, but revumenib is the first mutation-specific approved agent. AlloHCT in CR remains the standard consolidation for eligible adults.

Ruxolitinib cream (Opzelura) received FD: Ruxolitinib cream (Opzelura) received FDA approval (September 2022) for mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis; separately, ruxolitinib phosphate (Jakafi, oral) is FDA-approved for steroid-refractory acute/chronic GVHD but NOT specifically approved for CTCL as of 2026. However, the JAK/STAT pathway is aberrantly activated in MF/SS (~30–50% have JAK3 mutations or JAK1/STAT3/STAT5 alterations), making JAK inhibitors an active investigational area. Phase II evidence: ruxolitinib (oral) ORR ~29% in relapsed/refractory MF (RUXO-MF pilot data); itacitinib (JAK1 inhibitor) and cerdulatinib (JAK/SYK inhibitor) in phase II trials for CTCL. The CTCL-specific approvals are for non-JAK-targeted agents: romidepsin (HDAC inhibitor; FDA 2009 CTCL), brentuximab vedotin (CD30+; FDA 2017), mogamulizumab (CCR4; FDA 2018), vorinostat (FDA 2006). JAK3-mutant CTCL: JAK3 mutation identifies a subset with stronger a priori rationale for JAK inhibitor use; ESCAT IIA reflects absence of dedicated FDA approval in CTCL despite biological rationale and early phase data.

SC administration strongly preferred ove: SC administration strongly preferred over IV — equivalent efficacy with ~half the rate of grade ≥3 peripheral neuropathy. HSV/VZV prophylaxis with acyclovir is mandatory for the duration of therapy.
SC formulation strongly preferred from c: SC formulation strongly preferred from cycle-2 onward where available — substantially lower IRR rate (PALOMA-3 ~13% vs ~65% IV) and shorter administration time. Cycle-1 day-1 IV infusion split (350 mg → wait → remainder) reduces IRR severity. VTE prophylaxis (prophylactic-dose LMWH or DOAC for first 4 months) is mandated by the MARIPOSA / MARIPOSA-2 protocols when combined with lazertinib — VTE risk is substantially elevated vs ami or laz monotherapy. Premedication for IV (steroid + antihistamine + antipyretic) is non-negotiable. Aggressive EGFR-class skin care (clindamycin gel, oral doxycycline 100 mg BID prophylaxis, emollients, sun protection); paronychia: chlorhexidine soaks + high-potency topical steroid + careful nail care. Baseline workup: LFTs, albumin, CBC, ECG, pregnancy test, CT chest (ILD baseline). Monitor LFTs / CBC / albumin q2 wk first 8 wk then monthly; CT chest at any new respiratory symptoms. UA access via EAP / self-pay only.

SMARCB1 (INI1/hSNF5/BAF47) is a core sub: SMARCB1 (INI1/hSNF5/BAF47) is a core subunit of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex. Biallelic inactivation removes SWI/SNF antagonism of EZH2 (PRC2 complex), leading to H3K27me3 accumulation and epigenetic silencing of tumor suppressor genes. This makes SMARCB1-deficient tumors selectively sensitive to EZH2 inhibition. SMARCB1 loss defines three main tumor types: (1) Epithelioid sarcoma — tazemetostat FDA-approved (2020; EZH-202 trial). (2) Malignant rhabdoid tumor (MRT, AT/RT in CNS) — extremely aggressive; no approved targeted therapy; investigational EZH2 inhibitors. (3) SMARCB1-deficient chordoma, sinonasal carcinoma — rare. IHC for INI1 (nuclear loss) is the companion diagnostic for tazemetostat in epithelioid sarcoma and is simpler than molecular testing. Note: retained INI1 expression does NOT exclude epithelioid sarcoma — ~10% of cases have normal INI1 by IHC despite molecular loss (technical or heterogeneous loss).

SMO (Smoothened) is a G-protein-coupled: SMO (Smoothened) is a G-protein-coupled receptor that transmits Hedgehog (HH) signaling. Normally suppressed by PTCH1; activated when PTCH1 loses its inhibitory function (whether via PTCH1 loss-of-function or SMO gain-of-function mutation). SMO activating mutations (~10–20% of BCCs) and PTCH1 loss-of-function (~90% of BCCs) both result in constitutive HH pathway activation. Vismodegib and sonidegib are SMO antagonists — they bind the SMO transmembrane domain and block downstream HH signaling (GLI1/2 repression). In practice, BCC HHI therapy does not require pre-testing for SMO vs PTCH1 mutation — all BCCs have HH pathway activation. SMO mutations also occur in sporadic medulloblastoma (SHH subtype) and rarely in other tumors. Resistance: secondary SMO mutations (D473H most common) emerge during vismodegib therapy, driving acquired resistance. Sonidegib may be active in some vismodegib-resistant D473H mutants.

Cinacalcet is the only FDA-approved medical therapy specifically labeled for hypercalcemia of parathyroid carcinoma. It has no cytostatic/cytotoxic effect on the tumor — it controls the biochemical consequence (PTH-driven hypercalcemia) in unresectable, recurrent, or metastatic disease. SUFU germline pathogenic variants cause a Gorlin-syndrome–like predisposition with much higher medulloblastoma risk than PTCH1 (~30% lifetime vs ~5% in PTCH1), and lower BCC burden. SUFU-driven medulloblastomas cluster in the SHH-activated molecular subgroup (infant/young-child onset, desmoplastic / MBEN histology in many cases). Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per Foulkes et al. 2017 / AACR Pediatric Predisposition Working Group): brain MRI q4mo from diagnosis through age 3, q6mo from age 3-5, annually to age 8 — denser-than-PTCH1 cadence reflects higher MB risk. Dermatology surveillance for BCC q6-12mo from puberty. Avoid craniospinal external-beam radiation when alternatives exist (second-malignancy risk in carriers). Hedgehog-pathway inhibitors (vismodegib, sonidegib) have limited activity in SUFU-mutant SHH-MB — downstream-of-SMO position renders SMO inhibitors ineffective; this is a critical distinction from PTCH1-driven disease. ESCAT IIA.

Adenoid cystic carcinoma ~15% NOTCH1 mutant — AL101 / brontictuzumab in trials; otherwise cisplatin-based chemo modest activity. Comprehensive histology + molecular profiling at diagnosis is now ESMO-recommended for advanced salivary cancer.

USPSTF 2018: Grade C for men 55-69 (individualized shared-decision-making about benefits + harms); Grade D for men ≥70 (recommend AGAINST routine screening). NCCN 2025 (Early Detection): baseline PSA + DRE discussion at age 45 for African American men or BRCA2 carriers (high-risk groups), age 50 for average risk; if PSA <1 ng/mL, repeat every 2-4 years; if PSA 1-3 ng/mL, repeat every 1-2 years; if PSA >3 ng/mL, evaluate further (repeat PSA, mpMRI, biomarker reflex such as 4Kscore/PHI, possible biopsy). Higher screening intensity for confirmed BRCA2 germline carriers (IMPACT study — PSA q1y starting age 40; biopsy threshold ≥3 ng/mL). PSA can be falsely elevated in BPH, prostatitis, urinary retention, recent instrumentation. Free PSA ratio, PSA density, and reflex biomarkers (PHI, 4Kscore, SelectMDx) reduce unnecessary biopsy. Limitations: overdiagnosis/overtreatment of indolent cancers (well-characterized harm — driver of USPSTF Grade C). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

Second most common IDH1 variant. Distrib: Second most common IDH1 variant. Distribution differs by disease: R132C is the dominant IDH1 variant in cholangiocarcinoma (~25-30% of IDH1-mutant CCA per ClarIDHy) and chondrosarcoma; in glioma it is rarer than R132H (<5%); in AML R132C accounts for ~30% of IDH1 mutations. Critically, R132C is IHC-NEGATIVE with the R132H-specific antibody (clone H09) — relying on IHC alone misses these patients. Ivosidenib (Tibsovo) is approved for IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma (ClarIDHy 2L+) and IDH1-mutant AML (AGILE in combination with azacitidine 1L unfit; monotherapy R/R) — labels cover all IDH1 variants on the proven hotspot list (R132C/R132G/R132H/R132L/R132S), not just R132H. Second of three Ashkenazi Jewish founder: Second of three Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutations. Single-nucleotide duplication (cytosine) in exon 20 causing frameshift and premature termination — truncates BRCA1 within the BRCT2 domain, abolishing C-terminal protein-binding function critical for homologous-recombination repair coordination. Also called 5382insC in legacy nomenclature (offset by stop-codon counting convention shift). Recurrent founder effect in AJ populations (~0.8-1.0% carrier frequency in AJ vs <0.1% non-AJ); also reported as a recurrent variant in Polish, Russian, Belarusian populations (likely separate founder events or AJ admixture). Lifetime cancer risks consistent with BRCA1 average. NCCN 2025 endorses population-wide AJ founder-panel testing (3-mutation panel) regardless of family history. Same surveillance and risk-reduction protocols as other BRCA1 pathogenic variants. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

Short half-life (~2.5-6 h) gives titratable BID dosing — characteristic patient-specific dose escalation based on blood-pressure response (titrate up to 10 mg BID if BP tolerable at 5 mg). A single IV or oral dose covers both acute (0-24 h) and delayed (24-120 h) phases of CINV. Approved by FDA July 2003 and EMA March 2005.

Serum AFP is used in combination with ultrasound every 6 months for HCC surveillance in cirrhotic patients of any aetiology (Child-Pugh A/B7, candidates for treatment) and in non-cirrhotic chronic HBV with elevated HCC risk per AASLD HCC 2023. US-alone sensitivity is suboptimal (~63%); US + AFP raises sensitivity for early-stage HCC to ~70-80% with acceptable specificity (~85-90%). AFP threshold typically >20 ng/mL (some guidelines >7 ng/mL with risk-stratified cutoffs). Rising AFP trajectory is more informative than single value. AFP elevation also occurs in chronic hepatitis flares, regenerative nodules, germ-cell tumours, and gestation — interpret in context. Diagnostic workup of rising AFP: multiphasic CT or MRI per LI-RADS criteria. AFP-L3 fraction and DCP (PIVKA-II) are adjunct markers in some practices. ESCAT IIIA — AFP directs HCC diagnostic workup / surveillance cadence.

Serum calcitonin is a highly specific biomarker for medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) — produced by parafollicular C-cells. In MEN2 RET germline carriers, calcitonin trends inform timing of prophylactic thyroidectomy (RET codon-stratified per ATA Thyroid 2015 + Endocrine Society MEN 2023): - MEN2B (M918T): prophylactic thyroidectomy <1 year, before calcitonin rise becomes detectable - MEN2A high-risk codons (634, 883): thyroidectomy by age 5 - MEN2A moderate-risk codons (609, 611, 618, 620, 630, 631): may delay until calcitonin becomes detectable on stimulation testing Basal + stimulated (pentagastrin / calcium-stimulated where available) calcitonin tracks residual disease post-thyroidectomy. CEA is a complementary marker. Doubling time of calcitonin post-resection is a strong prognostic indicator (<6 mo = aggressive). ESCAT IIIA — calcitonin directs prophylactic surgery timing and post-operative monitoring.

Uso di sorveglianza PRIMARY: dopo la resezione curativa-intenzionale del CRI stadio II/III — q3-6 mesi CEA per 2 anni poi q6 mesi per 3-5 anni (concordante NCCN/ESMO), crescente tendenza innesca l'esame dell'immagine per la ricorrenza. Due aumenti consecutivi >5 ng/ml o raddoppiamento entro 1-2 mesi giustificano la TAC toracica/abdomen/pelvis e considerano colonoscopia. Circa il 30% dei CRC non segretano CEA (miscrosatellite-instabile, mucinosa, ring-signet istology); in quei pazienti la sorveglianza CEA ha un rendimento limitato. Distinto da BIO-CTDNA-MRD che offre maggiore sensibilità analitica per la malattia residua molecolare. STUB in attesa di due-Co-Lead firma.

Primary utility: response monitoring in established metastatic disease (rising trend may precede imaging progression by weeks to months). Can be falsely elevated in benign breast disease, liver disease, ovarian cancer, and some lung cancers. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

Shimoyama smoldering or chronic-favourable subtype of ATLL. Smoldering: ≥5% circulating abnormal lymphocytes, no organ involvement (skin/lung lesion permitted), LDH normal, BUN normal, albumin normal, no hypercalcemia, no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. Chronic-favourable: similar to smoldering but lymphadenopathy/organomegaly permitted, LDH ≤2× ULN, BUN ≤ULN, albumin ≥ULN, Ca normal, no CNS/bone/GI/effusion. AZT+IFN-α (anti-HTLV-1 mechanism) yields 5-yr OS ~46% vs ~20% for chemotherapy in these subtypes (Bazarbachi 2010 meta-analysis, JNCI). Aggressive subtypes (acute/lymphoma/chronic-unfavourable) do NOT respond to AZT+IFN — route those to CHOEP+mogamulizumab via RF-ATLL-HIGH-RISK-BIOLOGY.

Sirolimus (rapamycin), an mTORC1 inhibitor, is FDA-approved (May 2015) and EMA-approved (2017) for treatment of LAM in adults. MILES phase III RCT (McCormack et al., NEJM 2011): N=89 (46 sirolimus, 43 placebo); 12-month treatment + 12-month observation. Primary endpoint: FEV1 change from baseline to 12 months (mL/month rate). FEV1 slope: +1 mL/month (sirolimus) vs -12 mL/month (placebo); difference 11 mL/month (p<0.001). Secondary: FVC improvement, VEGF-D reduction, 6-min walk improvement, QoL. After 12-month observation: benefits partially lost (FEV1 decline resumes), suggesting need for continuous therapy. mTOR inhibition does not eliminate LAM cells but controls their mTORC1-driven proliferation. Everolimus is used for TSC-associated LAM and for renal angiomyolipoma (EXIST-2). VEGF-D ≥800 pg/mL is a diagnostic biomarker (non-invasive diagnosis of LAM possible in right clinical context without biopsy).

Square-planar platinum(II) coordination: Square-planar platinum(II) coordination complex. After cellular uptake and aquation (Cl displaced by water in low-chloride intracellular environment), the activated species forms intra- and inter-strand DNA cross-links, predominantly 1,2-d(GpG) and 1,2-d(ApG) adducts. These adducts distort the DNA helix, blocking replication and transcription, and trigger apoptosis when not repaired. Resistance mechanisms include enhanced nucleotide excision repair, glutathione detoxification, and reduced cellular uptake (CTR1 transporter). Backbone for esophageal CRT, head-and-neck CRT, NSCLC, gastric (legacy), cervical, ovarian, testicular germ-cell, and bladder.

Standard H2 component of chemotherapy pr: Standard H2 component of chemotherapy premedication, paired with H1 antihistamine (diphenhydramine) and corticosteroid (dexamethasone). Particularly important before paclitaxel (Cremophor vehicle hyper- sensitivity), rituximab, daratumumab, and other monoclonal antibodies with significant infusion reaction rates. Standard adjunct for bronchospasm compon: Standard adjunct for bronchospasm component of anaphylaxis, chemotherapy infusion reactions, and CAR-T cytokine release syndrome — given concurrently with epinephrine (epinephrine remains the FIRST-LINE for true anaphylaxis with hypotension or upper airway edema). Nebulized 2.5-5 mg q20min × 3 then q1-4h is standard for moderate-severe bronchospasm. Critical: salbutamol does NOT reverse hypotension or upper airway edema — if these are present, epinephrine IM thigh is mandatory and urgent. Add ipratropium 500 µg nebulized if bronchospasm refractory or severe (combined β2 + muscarinic blockade). For bronchospasm during paclitaxel, rituximab, or monoclonal antibody infusions: stop infusion, administer salbutamol nebulized, diphenhydramine + famotidine + steroid as supportive — escalate to epinephrine if hypotension / upper airway involvement / no response in 5-10 min. Avoid in patients with cardiomyopathy / serious arrhythmia (QT-prolonging chemotherapy regimens particularly — TKIs, arsenic trioxide). Tachycardia and hypokalemia are dose-related — monitor in continuous nebulization. Ukraine: cheap, ubiquitous, NSZU-covered.
Standard adjunct for chemotherapy infusi: Standard adjunct for chemotherapy infusion reactions and severe anaphylaxis — given AFTER epinephrine IM (epinephrine is first-line, no substitute). Hydrocortisone's onset is delayed (4-6 h) so it prevents biphasic anaphylaxis recurrence rather than treating the acute event. Premedication for chemotherapy (e.g., taxanes, rituximab, daratumumab): typically dexamethasone 20 mg IV is used rather than hydrocortisone — dex is more potent (×30) per mg, has longer duration, lacks mineralocorticoid effect (less fluid retention), and dosing schedule is established. Hydrocortisone preferred over dex / methylprednisolone for: (1) adrenal insufficiency / crisis (mineralocorticoid activity matches physiological need); (2) septic shock with vasopressor refractoriness (300 mg/day approximately physiologic stress dose); (3) acute high-dose adjunct for refractory infusion reaction where mineralocorticoid effect supports hemodynamics. Single bolus of 100-200 mg has minimal long-term consequences — no taper needed for ≤3 days of acute use. Ukraine: cheap, ubiquitous, NSZU- covered.
Standard adjuvant for stage III colon, a: Adjuvante standard per colon stadio III, anche stadio II ad alto rischio (T4 / invasione linfovascolare / < 12 LN campionato / scarsamente diff). Substituted benzamide that antagonizes d: Benzamide sostituita che antagonizza i recettori dopaminergici D2 centralmente nella zona chemioreceptrice (area postrema) e perifericamente nel tratto GI superiore, riducendo la nausea e accelerando lo svuotamento gastrico. Inoltre un agonista dei recettori 5-HT4 (rilascio potenziale di acetilcolina nel plexo enterico → peristalsi aumentata) e ad alte dosi (≥1 mg/kg) un antagonista debole 5-HT3. L'azione procinetica lo distingue dagli antagonisti puramente D2 ed è terapeuticamente utile per la gastroparesi indotta da chemioterapia, lo svuotamento gastrico ritardato indotto da oppiacei e la dispepsia post-trattamento. Approvata dalla FDA nel 1979 per nausea/vomito e gastroparesia; ampiamente utilizzata come antiemetico di punta nei regimi CINV. Uso limitato nel 2009 (avvertimento FDA con cassetta) e 2013 (EMA) a causa del rischio di discinesia tardiva con impiego prolungato o ad alta dose.

Suicide enzyme-activated irreversible in: Inibitore irreversibile attivato da enzima suicida dell'ornitina decarboxilasi (ODC), il primo enzima limitante di velocità in poliammina (putrescina → spermidina → spermina) biosintesi. L'appagamento di poliammine sopprime la proliferazione cellulare. Logica di prevenzione del cancro: ODC è un bersaglio c-Myc; le poliamme sono elevate in adenomi colorrettali e molti tumori. PACES (Fase III, Meyskens et al.): eflornitina 500 mg + sulidac 150 mg PO al giorno ha ridotto gli adenomas metacronici di ~70% in 36 mesi in pazienti con adenamo colonici sporadici precedenti (Cancer Prev Res 2008); follow-up in corso. Approvato dalla FDA (Iwilfin, 2024) per la terapia di mantenimento di neuroblastoma ad alto rischio — prima indicazione oncologica per l'agente.
Sulfoxide prodrug reduced by gut microbi: Sulfoxide prodrug reduced by gut microbiota and hepatic enzymes to active sulindac sulfide, which non-selectively inhibits COX-1 and COX-2, suppressing prostaglandin (especially PGE2) synthesis. Cancer- prevention rationale: COX-2 is upregulated in FAP adenomas; sulindac reduces polyp number and size in FAP (Giardiello NEJM 1993 RCT — 150 mg BID for 9 months, ~56% reduction in polyp number, ~65% in size; pooled trials in retained rectum post-colectomy show similar effect). PACES RCT (Meyskens 2008) combined eflornithine + sulindac reduced sporadic colorectal adenoma recurrence by ~70%. NOT FDA- labeled for chemoprevention; used off-label per NCCN Genetic Familial Colorectal 2025 in selected FAP patients (e.g., retained rectum, duodenal disease) under specialist hereditary-CRC team supervision.

Direction HOLD on systemic therapy start until ICP controlled; priority 14. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff.

Synthetic 39-amino-acid peptide that act: Peptide sintetico 39-amino-acido che attiva sia polipeptide insulinotropico (GIP) di dipendenza glucosica e recettori GLP-1. Dual agonism produce un maggiore controllo glicemico e perdita di peso rispetto al monoagonismo GLP 1. Alla dose di obesità (max 15 mg settimanale), SURMUNT-1 ha dimostrato ~21% perdita di massa media vs ~3% sul placebo — superiore a semaglutide 2,4 mg. L'obesità è associata a 13+ tumori (IARC/WCRF) — perdita dipeso sostenuta è un intervento di prevenzione del cancro.

Synthetic broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone: fluorochinolone sintetico a ampio spettro che inibisce due topoisomerasi batteriche essenziali di tipo II: la ginasi del DNA (topoisomerasa II) — bersaglio primario nei batteri Gram-negativi — e la topoisomerosi IV — bersone primario nei bacteri Gram positivi. L'inibizione previene il supercartaggio/scartamento del DNA necessario per la replica, la trascrizione e la riparazione, producendo effetti battericidi con uccisione dipendente dalla concentrazione (AUC/MIC > 100 per Gram negativa). Eccellente attività vs Pseudomonas aeruginosa (migliore delle fluoroquinolone più antiche), Enterobacterales (inclusi gli ESBL in alcune regioni), Haemophilus, patogeni intracellulari (Legionella, Chlamydia), micobacteria atipica, Bacillus anthracis. Modesta attività Gram-positiva (inferiore a più tardi fluorochinolone). Circa il 70% biodisponibilità orale — IV---PO step-down conveniente. FDA-approvato 1987.

Synthetic imidazoquinoline TLR7 agonist. Binds TLR7 on plasmacytoid dendritic cells and monocytes/macrophages, triggering NF-κB-mediated release of IFN-α, TNF-α, and other pro-inflammatory cytokines. Induces a local Th1-skewed innate + cell-mediated immune response against virally-infected or dysplastic epithelium; not directly cytotoxic or antiviral itself. Used topically for HPV-associated and field- cancerization lesions (external genital warts, actinic keratosis, superficial BCC) where local immune-mediated clearance is desired.
Synthetic monocyclic β-lactam antibiotic: Synthetic monocyclic β-lactam antibiotic that binds penicillin- binding protein 3 (PBP-3) of aerobic Gram-negative bacilli with high affinity, inhibiting cell-wall synthesis and producing bactericidal effect. Activity narrowly restricted to aerobic Gram-negative bacteria including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacterales (most), Haemophilus, Neisseria. NO activity against Gram-positive bacteria, anaerobes, atypicals. Unique monobactam structure does NOT cross-react with penicillin or cephalosporin antibodies in IgE-mediated hypersensitivity, making aztreonam the preferred Gram-negative β-lactam for patients with documented severe penicillin allergy (including anaphylaxis). The exception is ceftazidime, which shares the aminothiazolyl side chain — patients with confirmed ceftazidime hypersensitivity may also react to aztreonam. FDA-approved 1986.
